mainTopic: Who gets a share of the קרבנות (being fit to eat), and whether an אונן may touch קדשים
overview: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule that a כהן unfit for עבודה gets no share of the קרבנות. ריש לקיש brings the פסוק "הכהן המחטא אתה יאכלנה". Challenges from the whole משמר, a קטן and a בעל מום refine this: 'eat' means 'get a share', and "כל זכר בכהנים" adds the בעל מום as an exception. The גמרא asks why that פסוק adds a בעל מום and not a טבול יום. It answers by reasoning and, through רב יוסף, from the word יאכלנה: only a כהן fit to eat gets a share. ריש לקיש asks about a בעל מום who is טמא, and רב אושעיא asks about a טמא כהן serving on קרבנות ציבור. A ברייתא about a כהן גדול who is an אונן answers both: a share requires being fit to eat right now. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's rule that an אונן may touch קדשים and works through a contradiction from a משנה in חגיגה. That leads to רבי ירמיה's idea that a person can guard himself only partly, and a ברייתא proving it begins at the end of the amud.

steps.title: What is the source for the משנה's rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that a כהן unfit for עבודה does not share in the קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the source in the תורה for the משנה's rule. This sets up ריש לקיש's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that a כהן who cannot do the עבודה does not get a share of the meat. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
From where do we know these things? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: Gemara: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: 'These matters' means the משנה's rule that a כהן unfit for the service does not get a share of the meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches that a כהן unfit for עבודה does not share in the meat

steps.title: ריש לקיש brings the פסוק about the כהן who does the atonement
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns from "הכהן המחטא אתה יאכלנה" that only the כהן who does the atonement eats.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: The פסוק says, "The כהן who brings atonement with it shall eat it." The כהן who brings atonement eats, and one who does not bring atonement does not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers with a פסוק about the חטאת. He reads it to mean that only a כהן who does the atonement eats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links eating with doing the עבודה. ריש לקיש reads this as a rule in both directions: if you do the חיטוי, you eat, and if you don't, you don't eat.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who brings atonement, meaning the כהן who does the עבודה of the חטאת
As the פסוק says

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
As the verse states:
"The priest who effects atonement with it shall eat it"
A priest who effects atonement shall eat;
one who does not effect atonement does not eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק "הכהן המחטא אתה יאכלנה" teaches that only one who does the חיטוי eats

steps.title: But the whole משמר eats without doing the service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש's rule: all the כהנים of the משמר eat, even though only one of them did the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really a rule? But the whole משמר does not bring the atonement, and they still eat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks ריש לקיש's reading. Many כהנים eat a חטאת even though they did nothing in its עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one כהן sprinkles the blood of each חטאת, yet every כהן in that week's משמר eats from it. So 'only the one who did the service eats' cannot be read literally.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed rule
The group of כהנים on duty in the בית המקדש that week

phrases.english: And is this a principle?!
But there is the entire priestly watch,
who do not effect atonement, and yet they eat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's literal reading that only the actual מחטא eats
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counterexample: the whole משמר eats without performing the חיטוי

steps.title: The rule means anyone fit to do the service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא clarifies that the פסוק means a כהן who is fit to bring atonement, even if he did not actually do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: We mean someone who is fit to bring atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by making the rule broader. Being fit for the עבודה is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule changes from 'the one who actually did it' to 'anyone who could have done it.' Now the whole משמר is included, since they are all fit to serve.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit to perform the atonement service
We are saying, or we mean

phrases.english: We mean one who is fit for effecting atonement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the כהן who actually did the חיטוי eats
steps.terutzMaskana: Any כהן fit to do the חיטוי eats

steps.title: But a קטן eats even though he cannot serve
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new version: a young כהן is not fit to serve, yet he eats קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a קטן is not fit to bring atonement, and he still eats!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the corrected rule from step 4. A child כהן cannot do עבודה, yet he is allowed to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If eating depends on being fit to serve, a קטן should not eat. But he does, so the rule still does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor, a child who has not yet come of age
But here is (a case that contradicts)

phrases.english: But there is a minor,
who is not fit for effecting atonement, and yet he eats!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי קָטָן דְּאֵינוֹ רָאוּי לְחִיטּוּי, וְאוֹכֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that only one fit for חיטוי eats
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counterexample: a קטן is unfit yet eats

steps.title: 'Eat' really means 'receive a share'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads יאכלנה as יחלקנה: only one fit to serve gets a portion, but others may still eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does "he shall eat it" mean? He shall get a share of it. One fit to bring atonement gets a share, and one not fit does not get a share.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes what the word 'eat' means in the פסוק. It means getting an official share, not the act of eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now a קטן fits: he does not get his own portion, but he may eat what others give him. Being fit for עבודה decides who gets a share, not who is allowed to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall eat it
He shall receive a share of it
Receives a share in the division of the meat

steps.confusionAlert: Eating and getting a share are two different things. A קטן may eat קדשים that are given to him, but he is not counted in the division.
steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק's 'eat' means 'get a share'. Being fit for the עבודה decides who shares in the meat, not who is allowed to eat it.

phrases.english: Rather, what is meant by "shall eat it"?
He shall receive a share of it.
One fit for effecting atonement receives a share;
one not fit for effecting atonement does not receive a share.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יאכלנה means the actual act of eating
steps.terutzMaskana: יאכלנה means receiving a share, and that depends on being fit for חיטוי
steps.whyThisMatters: This matches the משנה's wording, which speaks about getting a share (חולק) in the meat.

steps.title: But a בעל מום gets a share without being able to serve
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: a blemished כהן cannot serve, yet he gets a share.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a בעל מום is not fit to bring atonement, and he still gets a share!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule from step 6. A כהן with a blemish cannot serve, but he still gets a share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing 'eat' to 'get a share' does not help here. A בעל מום really is part of the division, even though he is not fit for חיטוי.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן with a physical blemish that disqualifies him from עבודה

phrases.english: But there is a blemished priest,
who is not fit for effecting atonement, and yet he receives a share!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי בַּעַל מוּם דְּאֵינוֹ רָאוּי לְחִיטּוּי, וְחוֹלֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that only one fit for חיטוי receives a share
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counterexample: a בעל מום is unfit yet receives a share

steps.title: A separate פסוק includes the בעל מום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the בעל מום is a special exception taught by "כל זכר בכהנים".
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה included the בעל מום: "Every male among the כהנים" comes to include a בעל מום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the בעל מום is a special exception taught by another פסוק. The general rule stays the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "כל זכר" make the group wider to include a blemished כהן. So the rule from יאכלנה still holds for everyone else, and the בעל מום gets a share only because the תורה added him on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
Included him
To include

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן fit for עבודה gets a share of the קרבנות. A בעל מום is the exception: he also gets a share, because "כל זכר בכהנים" includes him.

phrases.english: The Merciful One included a blemished priest:
"Every male among the priests"
comes to include a blemished priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special inclusion from a separate פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A בעל מום should not share because he is unfit for חיטוי
steps.terutzMaskana: A בעל מום shares because the תורה specifically included him through "כל זכר בכהנים"

steps.title: Maybe "Every Male" Includes a טבול יום Instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that "כל זכר" might add a טבול יום rather than a בעל מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that "every male" comes to include a טבול יום!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. Why say the extra words "כל זכר" add a בעל מום? Maybe they add a טבול יום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said "כל זכר" is a special exception for a בעל מום. But a טבול יום also cannot serve right now. So the extra words could just as easily be talking about him.

keyTerms.meaning: But say (suggesting a different reading)
Someone who went to the מקוה today but stays slightly טמא until nightfall
To include, to add to the rule

phrases.english: But say that "every male"
comes to include one who immersed that day!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges which case the extra words of step 8 are talking about.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that "כל זכר" adds a בעל מום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A טבול יום is also not fit to serve, so the extra words could be adding him instead.

steps.title: A בעל מום Makes More Sense Because He Eats
steps.stepSummary: It is more sensible to add the בעל מום, since he is allowed to eat קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the תורה would include a בעל מום, since he eats.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the בעל מום is the better choice. He is allowed to eat קדשים, while a טבול יום is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בעל מום cannot serve, but he is fully allowed to eat. A טבול יום cannot even eat right now. So it is more fitting to give a share to the one who can actually eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense, it stands to reason
Since, because

phrases.aramaic: מִסְתַּבְּרָא בַּעַל מוּם הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְרַבּוֹיֵי,
phrases.english: It stands to reason that it should include a blemished priest,
since he eats.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 by explaining why the בעל מום is the better choice.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "כל זכר" could add a טבול יום just as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: A בעל מום is the better fit because he is allowed to eat.

steps.title: On the Contrary, the טבול יום Will Be Fit Tonight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues the other way: the טבול יום is the better choice, since by evening he will be fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, it should include a טבול יום, since in the evening he will be fit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא flips the argument. The טבול יום has a strong point too: his problem ends tonight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בעל מום stays unfit to serve. A טבול יום becomes fully fit at nightfall. So maybe he is the one who deserves to be included.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
In the evening
He is surely fit

phrases.aramaic: אַדְּרַבָּה – טְבוּל יוֹם הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְרַבּוֹיֵי,
phrases.english: On the contrary, it should include one who immersed that day,
because in the evening he will be fit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the logic of step 10 around.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasoning that a בעל מום is the better choice
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The טבול יום's problem is only temporary, so he is closer to being fit than a בעל מום.

steps.title: Right Now He Is Still Not Fit
steps.stepSummary: Being fit later does not help. At this moment the טבול יום is not fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, in any event, he is not fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that what counts is right now. Right now the טבול יום is not fit, so the בעל מום stays the better choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The share is handed out now, and right now the טבול יום cannot eat. Being fit tonight does not change that. So the reasoning of step 10 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Now
In any event, at least

phrases.english: Now, in any event, he is not fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 and brings back the reasoning of step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The טבול יום should be included because he becomes fit tonight.
steps.terutzMaskana: What matters is the present, and right now he is not fit.

steps.title: רב יוסף: The Word "Shall Eat It" Teaches the Rule
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף learns from the word יאכלנה that only someone fit to eat gets a share.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Since יאכלנה means "shall get a share of it," the תורה should have written יחלקנה. Why write יאכלנה? To teach that one fit to eat gets a share, and one not fit to eat does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a different way to settle the question, straight from the wording of the פסוק. The תורה chose the word "eat" on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said יאכלנה really means יחלקנה, getting a share. If so, the תורה could have just written יחלקנה. Writing "eat" instead teaches that a share goes only to someone fit to eat. A בעל מום can eat, so he gets a share. A טבול יום cannot eat, so he does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, since (opening a logical argument)
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
Learn from it
Gets a share

steps.whatToRemember: Only a כהן who is fit to eat קדשים gets a share. So a בעל מום gets a share, but a טבול יום does not.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Now, what does "shall eat it" mean? "Shall get a share of it";
so let the Merciful One write "shall get a share of it"!
Why write "shall eat it"?
Learn from it: one who is fit to eat gets a share,
one who is not fit to eat does not get a share.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 9, based on the wording of the פסוק instead of logic.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the exact word of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "כל זכר" might be adding a טבול יום.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word יאכלנה limits the share to those fit to eat, so the טבול יום is left out.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: A Blemished כהן Who Is Also טמא
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש asks whether a כהן who is both a בעל מום and טמא gets a share.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש asked: A בעל מום who is also טמא, do they give him a share? Since he cannot serve and the תורה still included him, maybe being טמא makes no difference. Or maybe only one fit to eat gets a share, and he is not fit to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש opens a new question that mixes the two cases we just discussed. He lays out both sides, and רבה answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side: the תורה already gave a share to a בעל מום even though he cannot serve, so adding טומאה should not matter. The other side: the rule from step 13 is that only one fit to eat gets a share, and a טמא person cannot eat.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked, raised a question
What is the law?
What difference does it make to me
Or perhaps

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two problems. Being a בעל מום stops him from serving. Being טמא stops him from eating. The question is whether the second problem takes away the share the תורה gave him.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish raised a question:
A blemished priest who is also impure,
what is the law, do they give him a share?
Since he is not fit, and still the Merciful One included him,

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא, מָה לִי טָמֵא מָה לִי בַּעַל מוּם;
phrases.english: there is no difference: what does it matter whether he is impure or blemished?
Or perhaps, one fit to eat gets a share,
and one not fit to eat does not get a share?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question that tests the rule from step 13 on a mixed case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a כהן who is both a בעל מום and טמא gets a share of קדשים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This question tests whether the share a בעל מום gets is a full exception, or whether it still depends on being fit to eat.

steps.title: רבה proves you must be fit to eat right now
steps.stepSummary: רבה brings a ברייתא: a כהן גדול who is an אונן may bring קרבנות, but he does not eat and gets no share to eat that night. This proves that a share requires being fit to eat. So a בעל מום who is טמא gets no share.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Come and hear a ברייתא. A כהן גדול may offer קרבנות while he is an אונן, but he does not eat, and he does not get a share to eat in the evening. Learn from this that we require the כהן to be fit to eat. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers ריש לקיש's question from Step 14 by bringing a ברייתא about a כהן גדול who is an אונן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול who is an אונן is allowed to serve, and by evening he could even eat, yet he gets no share because right now he cannot eat. So a share depends on being fit to eat. A בעל מום who is טמא cannot eat either, so the inclusion from "כל זכר" does not help him, and he gets no share.

keyTerms.meaning: The High Priest
A mourner on the day a close relative died, before the burial
Fit to eat קדשים
Learn from it: used to state a proof, and repeated to agree with it

phrases.english: Rabba said: Come and hear:
A High Priest may offer sacrifices while a mourner,
but he does not eat,
and he does not get a share to eat in the evening.
Learn from this: we require him to be fit to eat!
Yes, learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's question from Step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A בעל מום who is טמא gets no share, because a share requires being fit to eat right now.
steps.whatToRemember: A כהן gets a share only if he can eat right now. Being able to eat later that evening does not count.

steps.title: Does a טמא כהן who serves on communal offerings get a share
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא asks about a טמא כהן who serves on קרבנות ציבור, which may be offered even in טומאה. Does he get a share because he does the atoning, or does he get none because he cannot eat?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא asked: a כהן who is טמא and serves on communal offerings, do they give him a share? Do we say the תורה said "the one who atones," and this כהן also atones? Or perhaps only one who is fit to eat gets a share, and one who is not fit to eat gets no share?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא asks a new question about a כהן who is טמא but is still allowed to serve, because the offering is a communal one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two possible rules here. One says that whoever does the service gets a share, from the word הַמְחַטֵּא. The other says that only someone fit to eat gets a share. In this case the two rules give different answers, because this כהן may serve but may not eat.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (an open question)
Communal offerings, which may be brought even in טומאה
The one who atones, meaning the כהן who does the service
Or perhaps
Receives a share

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya asked:
An impure priest serving on communal offerings,
what is the law, do they give him a share?
Do we say:
"The one who atones," the Torah said,
and this one also atones;
phrases.notes: Since communal offerings may be brought in טומאה, this טמא כהן is really doing the service.

phrases.english: or perhaps one who is fit to eat gets a share,
and one who is not fit to eat does not get a share?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question that tests the same rule about being fit to eat
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which rule decides who gets a share: doing the service (הַמְחַטֵּא) or being fit to eat?

steps.title: רבינא answers from the same ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבינא uses the same ברייתא about the כהן גדול who is an אונן. That כהן serves, yet gets no share because he cannot eat. So a טמא כהן on קרבנות ציבור gets no share either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Come and hear. A כהן גדול may offer קרבנות while he is an אונן, but he does not eat, and he does not get a share to eat in the evening. Learn from this that we require the כהן to be fit to eat. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers רב אושעיא's question by quoting the same ברייתא that רבה used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול who is an אונן is allowed to serve, so he counts as one who atones. Even so, he gets no share. This shows that serving is not enough, and he must be fit to eat. So the טמא כהן who serves on קרבנות ציבור also gets no share.

keyTerms.meaning: We require
In the evening, once the אנינות is over

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a copy of Step 15. The גמרא really does repeat the same ברייתא, because the same proof answers two different questions. ריש לקיש asked about a בעל מום who is טמא. רב אושעיא asked about a טמא כהן who may serve on קרבנות ציבור. In both cases the ברייתא shows that a share requires being fit to eat.

phrases.english: Ravina said: Come and hear:
A High Priest may offer sacrifices while a mourner,
but he does not eat,
and he does not get a share to eat in the evening.
Learn from this: we require him to be fit to eat!
Yes, learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אושעיא's question from Step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A טמא כהן who serves on קרבנות ציבור gets no share, because what counts is being fit to eat, not being able to serve.
steps.whatToRemember: Two things do not earn a share: being able to serve, and being able to eat only later. Only being fit to eat right now does.

steps.title: May an אונן really touch קדשים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה, which says an אונן may touch קדשים. It challenges this from another משנה, which says an אונן needs טבילה before dealing with קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: an אונן may touch, but he may not offer. Can an אונן really touch? But there is a contradiction from another משנה: an אונן and a מחוסר כיפורים need טבילה for קודש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to our משנה and points out that another משנה seems to say the opposite about an אונן touching קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה lets an אונן touch קדשים. The משנה in חגיגה says an אונן must first go to the מקוה before dealing with קודש. That suggests that without טבילה he may not touch it. The גמרא now needs to explain how the two fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: Touches
Offers a קרבן
And they set it against: a contradiction from another source
Someone who still has to bring a קרבן to finish becoming טהור
Immersing in a מקוה

phrases.english: "A mourner may touch but may not offer, etc."
A mourner may touch?!
But there is a contradiction:
A mourner and one who still lacks atonement
phrases.notes: This comes from a משנה in חגיגה 21a.

phrases.english: need immersion for holy things!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the גמרא goes back to the next line of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that an אונן may touch קדשים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in חגיגה says an אונן needs טבילה before dealing with קודש. That suggests he may not touch קדשים without it, which seems to go against our משנה.

steps.title: One משנה is about an אונן who immersed, the other about one who did not
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי in the name of רבי יוחנן answers the contradiction. Our משנה, which lets an אונן touch קדשים, is about one who already did טבילה. The משנה in חגיגה, which requires טבילה, is about one who has not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: There is no contradiction. Here he already immersed, and there he did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from Step 18 by saying the two משניות are talking about two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both משניות agree that an אונן needs טבילה before touching קודש. Our משנה permits touching because it is talking about an אונן who has already immersed. The משנה in חגיגה describes what he must do if he has not immersed yet.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This is the standard way to begin an answer to a contradiction.
Here... there. Used to split two sources into two different cases.
He immersed in a מקוה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
It is not difficult. Here, it is where he immersed,
phrases.notes: "Here" means our משנה, which lets an אונן touch קדשים.

phrases.english: there, it is where he did not immerse.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא; כָּאן בְּשֶׁטָּבַל, כָּאן בְּשֶׁלֹּא טָבַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each משנה describes a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות seemed to disagree about whether an אונן may touch קדשים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה is about an אונן who already did טבילה. The משנה in חגיגה is about one who did not.

steps.title: An אונן's immersion does not last, because his אנינות returns
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. What good is טבילה for an אונן? רבה בר רב הונא taught that when an אונן immerses, his אנינות returns to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he immersed, so what? His אנינות comes back on him. As רבה בר רב הונא said: an אונן who immersed, his אנינות returns to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 19. It argues that טבילה cannot help an אונן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 relied on the אונן's טבילה to permit touching. רבה בר רב הונא teaches that the אנינות status comes back on him even after he immerses. If so, his טבילה should not make him fit, and the split between 'immersed' and 'not immersed' falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: What of it? So what does it help?
The status of an אונן: a mourner on the day a close relative dies, before burial.
Returns to him; comes back on him.

phrases.english: And if he immersed, what of it?
But his acute mourning returns to him!
As Rabba, son of Rav Huna, said:
An acute mourner who immersed, his acute mourning returns to him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי טָבַל מַאי הָוֵי? הָא הָדְרָא עֲלֵיהּ אֲנִינוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's split between an אונן who immersed and one who did not (Step 19).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבה בר רב הונא, an אונן's אנינות returns after טבילה. So טבילה cannot be what lets him touch קדשים.

steps.title: It depends on whether he took his mind off guarding his purity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה in חגיגה is about an אונן who took his mind off guarding his purity. Our משנה is about one who kept his mind on it, so his טבילה still holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. That case is where he took his mind off it. This case is where he did not take his mind off it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the split from Step 19 by giving a new way to tell the two משניות apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new answer adds a further detail: whether the אונן stayed alert to guarding his purity. If he stayed alert, he may touch קדשים, as in our משנה. If he became distracted, he needs טבילה, as in the משנה in חגיגה.

keyTerms.meaning: He took his mind off it; he stopped paying attention to guarding his purity.
This one... that one. Used to split two sources into two cases.

phrases.english: It is not difficult. That is where he was distracted,
phrases.notes: "That" is the משנה in חגיגה, which says he needs טבילה.

phrases.english: this is where he was not distracted.
phrases.notes: "This" is our משנה, which lets him touch קדשים.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא; הָא דְּאַסַּח דַּעְתֵּיהּ, הָא דְּלָא אַסַּח דַּעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20 with a new way to split the two משניות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא) by the אונן's mental focus on guarding his purity.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because an אונן's אנינות returns, טבילה seemed unable to explain why he may touch קדשים.
steps.terutzMaskana: If he did not take his mind off guarding his purity, he may touch, as in our משנה. If he did, he needs טבילה, as in the משנה in חגיגה.

steps.title: Being distracted should require sprinkling, not just immersion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new answer. רבי יוסטאי בר רבי מתון taught in the name of רבי יוחנן that someone who took his mind off guarding his purity needs sprinkling on the third and seventh days. So why does the משנה in חגיגה require only טבילה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who took his mind off it needs sprinkling on the third and seventh days. As רבי יוסטאי בר רבי מתון said in the name of רבי יוחנן: one who took his mind off it needs sprinkling on the third and seventh days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 21. It argues that a distracted person needs much more than טבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who took his mind off guarding his purity is treated as if he might have become טמא מת. That kind of טומאה needs sprinkling on the third and seventh days. Yet the משנה in חגיגה requires only טבילה, so it cannot be talking about a distracted person.

keyTerms.meaning: Distraction; taking one's mind off guarding one's purity.
Sprinkling, here with the purifying water used for טומאת מת.
The third and seventh days, when a טמא מת is sprinkled.

phrases.english: Distraction requires sprinkling on the third and seventh days,
as Rabbi Yustai, son of Rabbi Matun, said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: הֶיסַּח הַדַּעַת – צָרִיךְ הַזָּאָה שְׁלִישִׁי וּשְׁבִיעִי!
phrases.english: Distraction requires sprinkling on the third and seventh days!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 21 that the משנה in חגיגה is about an אונן who took his mind off guarding his purity.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן rules that היסח הדעת requires sprinkling on the third and seventh days. The משנה in חגיגה requires only טבילה, so it cannot be describing a distracted person.
steps.confusionAlert: This step is not the end of the discussion. It raises a new problem with the answer from Step 21, and the next step responds.

steps.title: Corpse impurity versus creeping-animal impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 22. רבי יוחנן's rule requiring sprinkling is about someone who stopped guarding against טומאת מת. The משנה in חגיגה is about someone who stopped guarding only against טומאת שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. That ruling (sprinkling on the third and seventh days) is about someone who took his mind off guarding against corpse impurity. This ruling (only טבילה) is about someone who took his mind off guarding against impurity from a creeping animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא splits the two rulings by the kind of impurity the person stopped guarding against.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sprinkling (הזאה) is only needed for טומאת מת. So if the אונן in חגיגה only stopped watching out for טומאת שרץ, he would not need sprinkling, just טבילה. That would explain why the משנה mentions only טבילה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. The opening of an answer that resolves a contradiction.
He took his mind off it. He stopped paying attention to guarding his purity.
Impurity from a dead body. Removing it needs sprinkling on the third and seventh days.
Impurity from touching a dead creeping animal. This is a lighter impurity that needs no sprinkling.

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
that one is where he took his mind off impurity from a corpse,
phrases.notes: 'That one' is רבי יוחנן's rule from Step 22, which requires sprinkling.

phrases.english: this one is where he took his mind off impurity from a creeping animal.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the משנה in חגיגה, which requires only טבילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא; הָא דְּאַסַּח דַּעְתֵּיהּ מִטְּמֵא מֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 22 by separating the two rulings into different cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Split cases (אוקימתא): each source deals with a different type of impurity.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anyone who took his mind off guarding his purity needs sprinkling, so the משנה in חגיגה is incomplete.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sprinkling applies only to someone who stopped guarding against טומאת מת. The משנה in חגיגה is about someone who stopped guarding against טומאת שרץ.

steps.title: Creeping-animal impurity would need sunset and would forbid תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the answer twice. First, a person impure from a שרץ is fully impure and needs to wait for sunset, not just do טבילה. Second, he would be forbidden even to eat תרומה, so why does the משנה mention only קודש?
steps.simpleTranslation: A person impure from a creeping animal is truly impure. He needs to wait for sunset! And furthermore, he should be forbidden even in תרומה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows two problems with saying the משנה in חגיגה is about טומאת שרץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real טומאת שרץ is not removed by טבילה alone. The person stays impure until nightfall (הערב שמש), but the משנה mentions only טבילה. Also, real טומאה forbids תרומה too, yet the משנה in חגיגה speaks only about קודש, as a special extra strictness.

keyTerms.meaning: Fully, truly impure, not just impure because of an extra strictness.
Sunset. A person who did טבילה stays impure until nightfall.
The portion of produce given to a כהן. It must be eaten in purity, but its rules are less strict than קודש.
And furthermore. It adds a second challenge.

phrases.english: One impure from a creeping animal
is fully impure,
he needs sunset!
phrases.notes: The משנה in חגיגה mentions only טבילה, not waiting until nightfall.

phrases.english: And furthermore, even תרומה too!
phrases.notes: He means: such a person should be forbidden in תרומה too, yet the משנה speaks only about קודש.

steps.triggerLanguage: טְמֵא שֶׁרֶץ – טָמֵא מְעַלְּיָיא הוּא, הֶעֱרֵב שֶׁמֶשׁ בָּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה in חגיגה is about someone who stopped guarding against טומאת שרץ.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Real טומאת שרץ needs sunset and also forbids תרומה. Neither fits the משנה in חגיגה, which requires only טבילה and speaks only about קודש.

steps.title: He guarded against impurity but not against what disqualifies
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה narrows the case. The person says he guarded himself from anything that makes him truly impure, but not from things that only disqualify him for קודש. So he needs only טבילה, and he is fine for תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: The case is where he says, 'I guarded myself from anything that would make me impure, but I did not guard myself from anything that would make me unfit.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה gives a new, narrower description of the person in the משנה in חגיגה to answer both challenges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he guarded against real טומאה, he is not truly impure. So he needs no sunset and is permitted in תרומה. He only failed to guard against things that make a person unfit for the stricter standard of קודש, and for that, טבילה alone is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: I guarded myself.
That makes me impure. Real טומאה.
That makes me unfit. Something that only disqualifies a person for holy things, without making him truly impure.

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer depends on a new idea: a person can guard his purity on one level and not on another. The next step questions exactly that idea.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
It is where he says: I guarded myself from anything that would make me impure,
but I did not guard myself from anything that would make me unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: בְּאוֹמֵר נִשְׁמַרְתִּי מִדָּבָר הַמְטַמְּאֵנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both parts of the קשיא in Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to someone who guarded himself only partly.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The person in חגיגה is truly impure from a שרץ, so he would need sunset and be forbidden in תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: He guarded against real טומאה, so he is not truly impure. He only failed to guard against things that disqualify for קודש, which טבילה alone fixes.

steps.title: Can a person guard himself only halfway?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether guarding one's purity can really be split in half: guarding against one kind of problem but not another.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is there such a thing as guarding halfway?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the idea that רבי ירמיה's answer depends on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think guarding your purity is all or nothing: either you are paying attention or you are not. If so, רבי ירמיה's case would be impossible. The גמרא wants to know whether partial guarding is a real concept.

keyTerms.meaning: But is there...? It questions whether something exists at all.
Guarding, watching over one's purity.
For half, partly.

phrases.english: But is there such a thing as guarding halfway?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the basic assumption behind רבי ירמיה's answer in Step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether partial guarding of purity is a real, accepted concept.

steps.title: Yes, and a ברייתא proves it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes, partial guarding exists, and begins quoting a ברייתא to prove it. The ברייתא opens with a case where a basket is still on a person's head.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. And it is taught in a ברייתא: The basket is still on his head...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says yes and starts bringing a proof. This is a setup line, and the ברייתא continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of just saying partial guarding exists, the גמרא brings an earlier source to back it up. The ברייתא's case about a person carrying a basket will show that guarding can apply to one thing and not another.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes.
Basket.

phrases.english: Yes; and it is taught:
the basket is still on his head

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 26 with yes and begins a proof.
steps.raayaObject: That partial guarding of purity is a real concept.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a person who still has a basket on his head, continued in the next section.
